title: The drag-select marquee vanishes when the mouse pauses rather than releases
detail: THE ROWS HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the real cause is worse. Not bound to pointerup: the marquee is drawn straight onto the canvas context by Fabric, is not part of the scene, and every full repaint erases it. The editor repaints the whole scene 30 times a second (editor-main starts startChartRefresh at rate 30), so the marquee survived about 33ms — one frame — and was then gone until the pointer moved again. That is exactly the reported symptom: flashing during a drag, gone when the pointer stops. The editor now holds the refresh for the duration of a pointer gesture. Live readings are not worth showing mid-drag anyway, and the first frame after mouse:up brings them current.
check: Reverted fix: the browser test fails with the upper canvas reading 0, i.e. no marquee at all after a 600ms pause. With the fix the same read is non-zero. Live by hand on a rebuilt bundle: held the pointer still mid-drag for 1.8s and the marquee is still drawn (vg-027-fixed-held.png), where before the pause it was absent (vg-027-held.png); CPU readings resumed after release, 26% then 41% then 46%.

title: The crop notice contradicts the geometry it describes
detail: WITHDRAWN — the notice was right and the report was my instrument error. Fabric anchors .left/.top, it does not read them as a box: a theme that omits originX/originY revives at originX center, so the object box runs -60.5 to 140.5 while the glyph run is at -60.5 to -38.5, genuinely off a 1920 artboard. The real defect found alongside it — a revived display had no artboard boundary at all, so objects painted over the letterbox bars while the notice said they were not shown — is fixed in 299c0bf, which added artboard-clip and artboard-crop coverage and the persist.ts boundary. Kept rather than deleted because the mistake is the reusable part: a notice that disagrees with the geometry is usually the reader, and the way to tell is to check which one Fabric actually honours.

title: Every unmatched host path serves the player
detail: CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it was not the fallthrough itself but serveStatic: an extension-less path was treated as a client route and fell back to the bundle index.html, so /play and /display resolved to the dashboard. A file with an extension never took that branch, which is why /theme.json had always 404d while /nope returned 200 with a live display. The editor needs its fallback — it is a client-routed app under /editor — and the player does not: it is one document, so only "/" may fall back. serveStatic now takes that as a parameter, true at the editor mount and false everywhere else. ADR-0018 already claimed this path, so the 404 that answers now says Not found. rather than a build hint that is not true.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected 200 to be 404 for /play. Live against a rebuilt host: /?data=live and /favicon.svg serve 200, while /play, /display, /nope and /theme.json all answer 404 Not found. 43 host tests pass.

title: A palette token's key and the name an author sees are different strings, and that is by design
detail: MEASURED on the built editor, three colours added in a row. Keys: colour, colour-2, colour-3. Names: New colour, New colour, New colour — and renaming the second to "CPU brand" left its key at colour-2 and the list showing "CPU brand · 0". So the reported shape is real and the defect it was filed as is not: the key is an internal id that §75 already rules is never renamed, and it NEVER REACHES THE AUTHOR. document.body.innerText contains neither colour-2 nor colour-3; they appear only as select value attributes in the HTML. The layer list shows the name, which is the string a person typed. The one residue worth keeping: every added colour carries the identical default name New colour, so three of them are indistinguishable until the author renames each.
check: Live in the built editor: after three adds the token select reads colour, colour-2, colour-3 while the visible labels read New colour, CPU brand, New colour, and a body-text scan for colour-2 and colour-3 returns nothing. Renaming moved the label and left the key alone, which is the id contract rather than a defect.

title: A text run could not be told not to print its unit, so the author got the unit twice
detail: REFUTED AS WRITTEN, and the real gap is narrower and now closed. The mechanism always existed: formatValueSegment reads run.unitDisplay ?? binding.unitDisplay, and the reference theme uses it — measured on the shipped Starter, cpu-card-value is a value run on cpu.load with unitDisplay none plus a literal % at the caption size, and its canvas text reads 47%, one percent sign. What did not exist was a control. unitDisplay was on the CHART bindings panel and absent from the TEXT RUN panel, so an author who wanted the reference pattern had no way to author it: set a reading and the unit printed itself, add a literal % beside it and the unit printed twice. REPRODUCED BY HAND on the rebuilt editor: set the run to Short and cpu-card-value renders 69%%, set it back to None and it renders 64%. The run panel now carries the same four options the chart panel has, Default/None/Short/Long. It writes the RUN rather than the binding, because a run own unitDisplay takes precedence — writing the binding is silently shadowed by exactly the theme this control exists to reproduce, which the first version did.
check: Red without the control: the new test fails with TypeError reading a null select. With it, 26 run-panel tests pass, and live in a rebuilt editor the run reads 47% at None, 69%% at Short and 64% back at None — the doubled unit, produced and then prevented by the control.

title: The Ctrl+N discard prompt times out waiting for a Discard button
detail: THE ROW WAS RIGHT AND IT WAS A TEST DEFECT, in three places rather than one. REPRODUCED: reference-theme.spec.ts times out on waiting for a Discard button inside a dialog that is already visible — because the dialog it found was the artboard SIZE CHOOSER, which has Cancel and Create. Measured by hand on the running editor: Ctrl+N on a changed document opens Choose an artboard size; the question about the changes, Save changes before opening another theme?, arrives only after Create is pressed. The test looked for Discard one step too early. The second failure was also stale: it asserted the scene still held the reference composition after New, but New is a blank theme of the chosen size and the reference is the separate New from starter command — measured, the canvas holds 0 objects after Create and Discard. The third was the status copy, New Fabric theme against the products New theme. All three call sites now go through one answerDialogIfShown helper that WAITS for the dialog rather than asking is it up right now, which is what an async dirty guard made unanswerable.

The test was waiting on the Discard button inside a dialog that was already visible, because the dialog it found was the artboard size chooser with Cancel and Create; pressing Ctrl+N twice is what reaches the discard prompt. With the helper it passes in 15.5s, the two dialog tests in editor.spec.ts still pass, and npm run lint is clean with no isVisible().catch races left in tests/e2e.

title: The crop frame is drawn a whole image up and to the left of the image it frames
detail: A Rect is anchored at its centre but getBoundingRect() reports a corner, so the frame begin() built sat at twice the offset: its top-left was the image top-left, putting the frame up and to the left by one full image width and height. Three of its four edges, and the crop handles on them, fell off the canvas, so the session read as a frame that could be grown but never cropped. Owner: crop-manager/index.ts begin().
check: Reverted fix: the crop-frame test fails on origin left/top. The frame bounding rect now equals the image bounding rect left, top and size.

title: The display tells a reader it has 30 sensors when it reads 19
detail: MEASURED on the Starter served by a live host: the stream was requested with 30 key entries covering 19 distinct sensors (cpu.load three times, gpu.load three, ram.used.percent three, and six more twice), and the availability strip read "2 of 30 sensors have no reading". startHostedTheme built its key list with a flat map and no Set, while the two other call sites that answer the same question — the editor private semanticKeys in editor-main.ts and requiredSemanticKeys for a ThemeDocument — both dedupe. The hosted path is the one a real deployed display takes, so the count a wall reader sees is inflated by how many objects happen to bind the same reading. The repeat request is the same defect: the display asks for the same sensor three times a second and nothing new comes back.
check: Reverted fix: 2 of 3 bound-keys tests fail. Live on the served Starter after a player rebuild: the stream requests 19 distinct keys with no repeats, and the strip reads 2 of 19 sensors where it read 2 of 30 - vg-053-sensor-count.png.

title: A missing file is reported as a bundle that was never built
detail: serveStatic sent one message for every file it failed to read, so "The player bundle is not built. Run: npx vite build packages/player" answered requests for a theme.json, a package zip and a stale chunk alike. MEASURED against a host with both bundles built: /theme.json, /assets/theme.zip, /assets/nope.js, /editor/assets/nope.js and /editor/nope.html all returned 404 with that text. The message is the one AGENTS.md itself sends people chasing, so following it rebuilds a bundle that is already there and returns the identical answer — the failure mode is a loop, not a delay. The message now says Not found. once the bundle entry exists, and the build hint is reserved for the case it is true of. ADR-0018 records why no static server upstream solves this shape.
check: Reverted fix: the built-bundle test fails on "expected the player bundle is not built not to contain is not built". Live against a rebuilt host with both bundles present: /theme.json, /assets/nope.js and /editor/assets/nope.js all answer 404 Not found., while / and /editor/ still serve.

title: A pasted image and a new group are listed by their uuid instead of a name
detail: MEASURED in the built editor: pasting a PNG added a row reading image-d8032a9b-438c-4a46-8d1e-b469d3fdad16, and grouping two cards added group-<uuid>, while an inserted Rectangle read Rectangle. object-name.ts states the contract plainly — absence of a name means fall back to the id — and the id of a freshly minted object is a uuid, so the two creators that set no name are the two the fallback cannot help. image-manager and grouping-manager were the only creators not going through newObjectName, whose own comment already named this failure. Both now call it; the words Image and Group live in ui-copy beside text and panel, where newObjectName already reads them.
check: Reverted fix: both tests fail on expected undefined to be Image and undefined to be Group. Live in a rebuilt editor: a pasted image row reads Image and a group built from a canvas shift-click multi-select reads Group, where both previously printed a 42-character id.

title: Filling in one Size field left half an authored box, and the text object lost its width
detail: MEASURED, and it destroys the object. A text inserted by the editor has no authored box — its width is Fabric measurement until an author types one. Typing 120 into Height wrote vigiliaText.box as { height: 120 } with no width; the merge in selection-inspector was correct, the box it merged into did not exist. The next text change made authoredBox multiply an undefined width by the scale, and the object ended with width null and getBoundingRect() returning nulls — unrenderable, unselectable by geometry, and no longer savable. Fixed by seeding both dimensions from the object own measured edge, so the first Size field an author fills in produces a whole box.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected undefined to be 126.21875, the measured width. Live on a rebuilt editor, the same sequence that ended at width null now reads width 63.8 and a bounding rect of 100x379, with vigiliaText.box holding both dimensions - vg-042-box-width.png.

title: Entering a group did not dim the layer list until something else re-rendered it
detail: MEASURED on the built editor: group two cards, double-click into the group, and 0 of 53 rows carry data-context. Click any row and 3 light up while 50 drop to opacity 0.45. CAUSE ESTABLISHED and it is not Fabric forgetting: entering a group does not move the selection. The group is already the active object, so setActiveObject is a no-op and MEASURED: zero of the four canvas events the bridge republishes on fire at all. The layer panel therefore never learns the context changed and keeps whatever projection it had. The manager now announces the context on the editor:group-context-changed canvas event — the custom editor: convention the other managers already use — and the bridge listens to it alongside its four.
check: Reverted fix: the announcement test fails on expected [] to have a length of 1. Live on a rebuilt bundle with real gestures: entering the group gives 3 rows in context and 50 dimmed, and double-clicking empty canvas returns to 0 and 0. 139 tests across the grouping and shell suites pass.

title: A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours
detail: MEASURED ON THE REFERENCE THEME, then fixed. The per-series paint is a positional array sitting beside the bindings, and removing a binding filtered the bindings without touching the paint. Measured on trends-chart: palette [cpu, gpu, ram] with bindings [trends-cpu, trends-gpu, trends-ram]; remove the MIDDLE one and the palette became [cpu, gpu] while the bindings became [trends-cpu, trends-ram] — so the RAM series painted with the GPU green. Nothing on screen looked wrong; the chart simply told a different story. seriesPaintFor already reconciled the arrays lengths and its truncation is right for the LAST binding, which is why the case nobody tries passes. The manager now carries each surviving series own paint through the removal before the length fix runs, so a middle removal keeps cpu and ram. Adding is unchanged: a new series repeats the last colour, which is what extending a chart means.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: trends-chart reads [palette.cpu, palette.gpu, palette.ram] before and [palette.cpu, palette.ram] after removing gpu.load, where it read [palette.cpu, palette.gpu] before the fix and painted RAM green. Two unit tests: carriedPaintFor pins the middle, the last and the unchanged case, and the panel test pins that the three Remove buttons name their reading and remove only their own. NOT PINNED: the one-line call from #writeBindings into carriedPaintFor — the manager-level test needs a panel harness this file does not have, and I did not build one. That wiring rests on the live measurement above, not on a test.

title: The palette colour field accepts anything, and persists it
detail: FIXED AT THE SOURCE, and the validator was not the gap. Measured first: the palette colour field accepted rebeccapurple, not-a-colour, #GGG and rgb(1,2,3) with no alert and checkValidity() reporting the field valid — and the published validator is no tighter, because validateGlobals checks the entry id, the name, that a value exists and that there are no unknown keys, and never looks at a colour. So the file the editor wrote passed its own schema because the schema has no rule. The field now asks the browser, which already holds the answer: CSS.supports("color", value) is the same engine that will paint it, so there is no second hand-written list of colour names to keep in step. A value the engine rejects is refused with the browsers own validity message naming it, and not committed — which matters because ctx.fillStyle keeps the PREVIOUS colour for an unparseable one, so accepting it meant the edit silently did nothing while the document carried the nonsense. STILL OPEN, deliberately: whether a CSS keyword such as rebeccapurple belongs in the vocabulary is a decision about which words the product accepts, not about correctness, and nothing here settles it. Upstream of vg-031 stays true — a picker does not fix a write path that does not check.
check: Red without the guard: the browser test fails on validity.valid expected false received true. Live in the built editor: #123456 commits, not-a-colour leaves the field invalid with a message naming it, and after the panel redraws from the palette the field reads #123456 again — the refused value was never committed. jsdom has no CSS object, so this can only be pinned in a browser; the unit suite cannot cover the predicate.

title: A selected Line shows a diagonal bounding box instead of two end handles and a rotate handle
detail: BUILT, after the search in ADR-0020 and a correction to it. A Line now carries two endpoint controls and the rotation handle — endpointA, endpointB, mtr — and no bounding box at all: hiding the six handles it does not need would have left the box, which is the defect. Each endpoint reads its own corner from x1/x2 and y1/y2 rather than assuming top-left and bottom-right, because width and height are absolute: measured on a line drawn right-to-left, the same two numbers are the other pair of corners. Moving an end writes that end and leaves the other where it was. Shift holds the line at a multiple of 15 degrees, on a modifier that branches in exactly one unrelated place. THREE THINGS THE ROW AND THE NOTE GOT WRONG, all found by measuring rather than reading. ONE: this projects Line is x1, y1, x2, y2 — four scalars, no points, no pathOffset, no setDimensions — so Fabric polyline controls and the anchor technique that go with them do not apply to it; nothing in snap-manager reads either representation, so snapping was never going to understand an endpoint for free. TWO: writing x2 makes Line re-derive left/top, so reading the objects own matrix back on every mousemove mapped each step through a frame the previous step had already moved — measured, the handle landed about 1.6x where it was dropped and a purely horizontal drag raised the far end by 188 units. The gesture frame is now taken once at mouse-down. THREE, and it is the one that would have shipped: Line.ownDefaults resolves up the prototype chain to the object every Fabric object shares, so assigning controls onto it took the handles off rectangles and text boxes too. Caught by an existing handle-size test, and assigned as a new defaults object now.
check: Red without the controls: all three new tests fail, the first on the control names. Live in a rebuilt editor: a selected Line reads endpointA, endpointB, mtr; a textbox, a rect and a chart each still read all nine with mtr. Dragging the far end 100 canvas px at 0.374 zoom moved x2 by 266.7 against 267.1 expected — 0.06 percent — with x1 and y1 unchanged, and with Shift held the line settled at 15.0 degrees. Editor suite 1041 across 84 files.

title: The Performance Trends panel does plot; the empty reading was a five-second-old source
detail: REFUTED, and the row own hypothesis was the right one. Measured against a live host rather than the preview source, after 18 seconds: history() over a 60-second window returns 42 points for each of cpu.load, gpu.load and ram.used.percent, every one status ok, and the panel draws all three lines - vg050-trends-live.png. The earlier reading of zero keys came from the PREVIEW source after 5 batches and 7 seconds, which is exactly the explanation the row offered when it filed itself as a measurement rather than a finding: chartPlaybackDelayMs exists on the source, so playback simply had not filled the window yet. The pass repeated mistake is closing here: two sessions read an empty source as a broken chart, and the thing that separated them was waiting longer and reading a real telemetry source, which is what this row said to do.
check: Live on a host streaming real telemetry: 42 points in the 60s window for each of the three series, latest 39.2, 30 and 83.6 percent, all status ok, and the panel draws three lines. The strip beside it reads 2 of 19 sensors have no reading, which is the LibreHardwareMonitor gap and not this.

title: The Starter was reported as edited the moment it opened
detail: FIXED, and the cause was not what two earlier readings of this row guessed. isDirty compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and the document differed from itself. THE INSTRUMENT THAT SETTLED IT, built in jsdom because a browser probe could not reach it: mount the Starter, snapshot, run one live pass, snapshot, and report the differing JSON paths. THE ANSWER IS styles. One pass rewrites .scene.objects.N.styles[M] on 18 of the Starter 52 objects — exactly its binding count — with nothing touched. styles is Fabric per-character formatting; the authored truth for a bound text object is vigiliaText.runs, and the renderer resolves runs into styles and text. documentKey now compares the document with those two renderings removed, on the objects whose runs are the authored truth; an object without runs owns its text and styles and keeps them. The asset half was fixed separately and is in the same commit — it enumerated the loaded byte map, so the key depended on how much had loaded rather than on what the document declares. NOT text, as I first assumed: stripping text alone changed nothing, and I reverted that rather than ship a key transform on an unproven hypothesis that could hide a real edit.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: Ctrl+N then Create on an UNTOUCHED Starter no longer asks to save. It still asks after inserting a Rectangle, and still asks after editing a text run by hand. title: The palette colour field has a picker that keeps alpha
detail: BUILT on shadcn, per the ruling that this fields ecosystem is shadcn/ui rather than Base UI; that ruling supersedes the plans 2026-09-29 search, which reached the opposite conclusion, and the plan is annotated so the question is not re-litigated. WHAT IT IS: a popover with four tracks — saturation, brightness, hue and alpha — over a checkerboard so a translucent token reads as translucent, a hex field for exact entry, and a swatch trigger beside the existing text field, which stays because a value can be typed exactly and a picker cannot always be dragged to it. Everything is 8-digit hex, which is what the envelope stores. WHY NOT A NATIVE INPUT, which is the requirement that rules the obvious answer out: input type=color has no alpha channel and the themes paints carry it — panel is 85 percent and frost is 30 percent — so accepting one would be a way to lose the value. THE COST, STATED ONCE: shadcn components are Radix-based, so this adds a second headless library beside Base UI, plus clsx, tailwind-merge and cva. The user ruled with that cost in view. The maths is a pure module with its own tests, away from the DOM: it caught two of my own bugs — alpha scaled as if it were a 0-255 channel, turning 85 percent into 1/255, and a regex capture passed where the parsed alpha belonged, producing NaN in the hex.

title: A binding no longer outlives its object, so deleting a readout does not disarm saving
detail: FIXED AT THE SERIALISER, not at the delete. A binding is keyed by its object id, so deleting the object left a key naming something the scene no longer had; serialiseThemeEnvelope then produced a document the validator refuses and every later save in that session threw with nothing in the UI saying so. The Starter binds 25 of its 52 objects, so deleting one sensor readout disarmed saving for the rest of the session while the row simply looked like it had vanished. snapshot now drops bindings whose key is not an object in the scene. WHY THERE AND NOT AT EACH DELETE: the keyboard, the layer list, the context menu, undo and any path added later all arrive at snapshot, so this cannot be the one that was forgotten, and it is a trust boundary — the serialiser no longer names an object that is not there, whatever removed it. A binding is meaningless without its object, so nothing is lost that the document could still use, and an author who re-adds an object with that id gets its reading back. THE ROWS OTHER TWO QUESTIONS ARE NOT ANSWERED and are still decisions: whether a save that throws should report itself rather than vanish, and whether a failed save leaves the document marked dirty so the author is warned on the way out. Both are separable from this and neither is fixed here.
check: Against a live host, the rows exact sequence: delete network-up, then File > Save to library. The host document now reads 51 objects with network-up absent, bindings 25 to 24, and no binding naming a missing object — and no pageerror. Red without the fix: the test fails with Invalid Fabric theme: Fabric object network-up is not in this scene, the exact error the row reported. Editor suite 1050 across 85 files.

title: A deleted object now disappears from the layer list, the canvas and the inspector together
detail: FIXED, and it was two subscriptions rather than one. A deletion fires no selection event — the active object is discarded first — so neither the bridge nor the selection inspector was told, and the row survived. Measured on the row own sequence: after Edit > Delete on network-up the canvas reported 51 objects and the host document agreed, but the layer list still showed 52 rows including network-up, and the inspector still read its name and geometry. So the three surfaces disagreed about what the document contained, and the row is right that this is one defect seen three ways. Both now subscribe to object:removed and object:added: the bridge, which republishes the layer projection, and the selection inspector, which re-binds its fields. After the same keystroke all three agree — 51 rows, no network-up, and the inspector empty. THE STUB WAS ALSO LYING, which is worth recording: bridge.dom.test.ts canvas stub answered getObjects but had no add or remove, so a test that deleted an object was still projecting from an array that still held it. A test written against that stub would have passed for the wrong reason — mine did, on the first attempt. The stub now has Fabric own add and remove, and the tests pin the republish rather than the projection, because layers() reads live and so was never the thing that was stale.

title: Insert > Text takes the caret, so the first keystroke lands
detail: FIXED, and the obvious fix was not the one that worked. insertNewText now enters editing and selects the new text, which is what every editor this product is measured against does when you ask for a text box. Calling it SYNCHRONOUSLY put the caret in and then lost it: the menu the insert came from takes focus back for itself as it closes, so a keystroke after Insert still went nowhere and document.activeElement was BODY. title: Release package and Open package both work; automation could not see either
detail: REFUTED IN FULL, and it is the most expensive instrument error on the pass: it would have had two working features fixed, and vg-034s rename applied to buttons that already do their job. Both commands are wired and both complete. Release package asks window.prompt for major/minor/patch and then downloads; answering it produces vigilia-demo-dashboard.vigilia-theme. Open package calls picker.click() and a native file chooser opens. THE ROUND TRIP THEY EXIST FOR WAS RUN END TO END: Release exported a package, that file was fed back through Open package, and the editor came back with 52 objects and 52 layer rows. WHY IT LOOKED INERT, twice over, and neither is the product. Release uses window.prompt, and automation DISMISSES it without being asked — the handler takes the null and returns early, so there is no download, no toast and no page error, which is precisely the signature filed as a dead command. Open package opens a native file chooser, which a script cannot observe at all. I hit this myself earlier in the same session: I triggered Release, could not answer the dialog, and recorded that the download never fired. The sibling Save package works because it has neither a prompt nor a chooser, which is why the comparison made the other two look broken. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is worth more than the row: a native prompt or a native chooser is invisible to automation and an auto-dismissed prompt is indistinguishable from an absent one. Any future finding of the form a command does nothing at all must first be checked for a dialog or a chooser in the way.
check: Live: Release prompts for a bump and downloads vigilia-demo-dashboard.vigilia-theme once answered; Open opens a native file chooser; that exported file fed back through Open restores 52 objects and 52 rows.

title: Each rail pane keeps the scroll offset you left it at
detail: FIXED IN THE LAYOUT, which is where the swap happens. The rail is single-panel, so opening Assets takes the layer list down and builds it again — and everything else survived that swap while the scroll did not, which is what made it worth separating: the selection stayed, the inspector kept its geometry, the canvas kept its handles. choosePane now reads the outgoing panels scroll offset off the DOM and restores the incoming ones a frame later, after the new content is laid out, or the offset would land on whatever height it has at that instant. Read off the DOM rather than kept in state on purpose: the panel is torn down by the swap, so anything held in state is gone by the time the next panes turn runs.

title: A rename changes the name and leaves the id, so it cannot orphan a binding
detail: REFUTED, and it is the same reading error as the other name-versus-id ones: the rows evidence searched the saved document for the new name and found the old id gone. MEASURED, on the rows own sequence — click network-down, Enter, type RENAMED-BOUND, Enter, File > Save to library. The saved object reads id network-down, name RENAMED-BOUND, and its binding is still keyed network-down still holding network.download; 52 objects, 25 bindings, and nothing dangling. A rename moves the DISPLAY NAME and leaves the id alone, which is the documented contract: the id is the stable key bindings, the schema path and the envelope carry. So there is no route by which renaming an object can orphan its binding, and the asymmetry the row describes — delete throws while rename saves a dangling document — cannot arise from this. Note what IS true and now covered either way: vg-059s serialiser drop would catch a rename that did re-key, because it drops any binding whose key is not an object in the scene. So this row was unreachable before the fix and harmless after it, which is why the earlier claim that the two paths end differently no longer holds either.

title: Collapsing or restoring a rail panel refits the theme to the space it freed
detail: FIXED, and the timing was the whole problem. Collapsing a panel hands the canvas 288px and the theme kept its zoom, so at a 1024-wide window the canvas grew from 370 to 658 and stayed at 22 percent — the freed space bought nothing. The viewport deliberately keeps its zoom across a resize, because a window nudge should not re-frame the theme, so the refit belongs on the panel toggle and not on the observer. It is done there by waiting on the viewport own change event, which is the signal that it has already resized. TWO WRONG VERSIONS FIRST, both worth recording because the second looked like a fix: one rAF fitted before the aside re-rendered, which fixed the collapse and left the restore at the collapsed zoom; two frames fitted before the viewports own ResizeObserver ran and did the same thing. Only the event is late enough to measure the new box. MEASURED at 1024 wide, the rows own case: 370 at 0.221, collapsed 658 at 0.394, restored 370 at 0.221. NOT PINNED BY A TEST, and the row should say so: the scroll half of this same commit is unit-tested and bites, but a refit test has to drive a whole React shell layout and the harness fought me for it, so I removed it rather than ship one that did not hold. The behaviour is verified in a browser, not by a unit test. HALF OF IT IS STILL OPEN AFTER THE FIX, re-measured by hand against cde9aa6 (collapsing a panel refits the theme to the space it freed) rather than taken from the agent's report. The panel half works: at 1024 the zoom badge reads 22%, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the badge to 39%, which uses the freed width. THE WINDOW-RESIZE HALF DOES NOT - that is vg-072, filed from the same sitting. Closing this row for the panel case is right; the resize case was folded into it and did not come with it.
check: Live at 1024x720: canvas 370px at zoom 0.221, collapsed 658px at 0.394, restored 370px at 0.221. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files.

title: The layer list answers the keys it declares by being a tree
detail: FIXED. The rows said the panel declares role=treeitem and answers to none of a trees keys, and that was right about the symptom and wrong about the cause: the code deliberately declined arrow keys, with a comment saying the window-level nudge handler owns them. THAT COMMENT WAS TRUE AND THE CONSEQUENCE WAS HIDDEN. The nudge defers only for a TEXT ENTRY — isTextEntryTarget — and a layer row is a div, so an unmodified arrow key was not blocked by the row, reached the nudge, and MOVED THE SELECTED OBJECT while the list did nothing at all. So the row was not merely missing keys, it was passing them somewhere worse. The row now takes ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End and ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, and stops propagation and prevents default, which is what lets the list be a list: navigation while focus is inside it, nudging while it is not. ArrowRight expands a collapsed group or steps into an expanded ones first child; ArrowLeft collapses or steps out to the parent, found by aria-level. MEASURED live with a real selection: from network-down, ArrowDown twice reaches network-card-icon, ArrowUp goes back, End reaches wordmark, Home reaches network-chart — and network-down is still at left 1355 top 702, where it was before any key was pressed.

title: A hidden layer is dimmed in the list, not only admitted by a tooltip
detail: FIXED, and it reuses a rule the stylesheet already had. The row measured a hidden row as identical to one that had never been touched — opacity 1 in both, same colour, nothing changed — with the eye buttons title the only tell. That is a mouse affordance for a state an author sets once and then forgets, and the list is the thing that should say what the canvas is doing. Rows now carry data-hidden, and the row dims on it with the SAME 0.45 an unreachable row uses for an entered group, because the two mean the same thing to an author: this is here but not available. MEASURED live: hiding cpu-card-icon through its own eye button takes the row to opacity 0.45 while gpu-card-icon beside it stays at 1. The rule deliberately does not stack with data-context=false, so a hidden row inside an entered group does not become 0.2 and unreadable. The test pins the ATTRIBUTE rather than a computed style, because jsdom applies no CSS and a computed opacity here would be a green test that proves nothing — the same trap as the marquee upper canvas and the bridge remove stub, both earlier today.

title: A focused layer row can be selected with the keyboard, so the list needs no mouse

A treeitem you can walk to but not pick is half a tree. Space selects the focused row, and Enter is deliberately left to rename, which already had it — so the two keys do not fight. title: A paired phone is served its own scripts, which it cannot carry a token for
detail: FIXED, AND IT IS THE PLAN FRAME BROKEN END TO END: a phone is the main display type, and a phone opening the hosts own pairing link got a blank page. REPRODUCED AND ISOLATED TO THE INTERFACE, not the phone: over LOOPBACK the same link renders the dashboard — 1 canvas, zero console errors, every asset 200 — while over the hosts LAN address the document is served and then everything it references is REFUSED. index-DKPxU5E6.js 403, echarts 403, favicon 403. THE CAUSE: the LAN guard sits before the static bundle routes, and a session token rides in the query string because fetch and EventSource carry one and script src cannot. So the guard was refusing the very request whose credential could never arrive. It was right about what it protects and placed too early. The bundle is not dashboard content — it is the same bytes any loopback visitor already has, with no reading, theme or device in it — so /assets/* and the favicon are now served ahead of the guard. Everything the guard exists for stays behind it: measured on an UNPAIRED device over the LAN, /api/themes/.../document 403, /api/display 403, /editor/ 403, /api/health 200, and the bundle 200. ADR-0019 records the search, including why the conventional answer — a cookie — is not this design, which pairs by a printed link with an expiring token.
check: Live: a paired phone at 390x844 over the LAN address renders the dashboard with 1 canvas and 0 console errors, where before the bundle and favicon were 403 and the page was blank. An unpaired device still gets 403 on the theme document, /api/display and /editor. Red without the exemption the test fails on the bundle being 403. Host suite 371 across 28 files.

title: The two Lines in the Insert menu no longer share a React key; their labels still do
detail: PARTLY FIXED, and the parts are worth separating. THE ROWS VISIBLE HALF IS WEAKER THAN FILED: the Insert menu DOES render group headings — Shape and Chart — so the chart Line is not unlabelled context, it sits under a Chart heading three items after Gauge. Measured live: thirteen items, Text then Shape then Chart, two entries reading Line. THE REAL DEFECT WAS UNDERNEATH IT, in the DOM rather than on screen: the item key was object.label, so a shape Line and a chart Line were two SIBLINGS WITH THE SAME REACT KEY, which is a reconciliation hazard rather than a cosmetic one. The key now carries what makes them different — shape:line and chart:line — so no two items in the menu can collide whatever they are called. title: A negative Size lands on the bound by ruling, and a test says why
detail: CONFIRMED AS FILED, THEN FOUND TO BE A RULING AND LEFT ALONE. The measurement holds: select storage-card-title, type -50 into Width, and the field and the object both read 1. But that is not an oversight — the repo decided it, wrote the decision down, and pinned it with a test whose comment names this exact case. refuses a value that would make the object invalid asserts that -5 lands on 1 and says why: it was restored to 40 with nothing recorded, and the floor is 1, so reverting is what made the bound undiscoverable. number-field.ts carries the same reasoning in code: Landing on the bound teaches it; reverting to the old value hides it. So the rows reading of AGENTS.md — refuse invalid numeric input rather than coercing — is about INVALID input, and the field does refuse it: X, 1e999, an empty string and 12.5.6 all leave the value untouched, exactly as the row itself measured. A negative size is a RANGE question the repo answered on purpose, not an invalid-input one, and reversing a considered ruling on the strength of a row that had not read the test would be wrong. I built the opt-in refusal, saw the existing test fail with expected 1 to be 240, and reverted. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING: the field is silent about the change. An author who types -50 and watches a 240-wide object become 1 wide gets no message, and whether that should be said is a smaller and better question than whether the value should be taken.

title: One Import asset click declares the file once
detail: FIXED, AND I CAUSED IT. The row found a real defect and it was mine, introduced by the vg-070 work earlier today: I moved the pane two-step place into AssetManager.placeImage so the assets pane and a pasted image would share one path, and forgot that the pane already did the import itself. placeImage imported again, so one Import click declared the file twice — the row measured three options from one import of one file, with one Image object on the canvas, which is the signature of a declaration made twice and a placement made once. MEASURED BEFORE, on the select options rather than a closed select innerText, which is the correction the row itself asked for: BEFORE one option, starter-backdrop; after ONE Import click, THREE options — starter-backdrop, the name, and the name with a -2 suffix. AFTER the fix, one click gives two options and one object, and a SECOND import of the same file is correctly its own asset at -2 rather than a phantom. The fix is that placeImage takes the declaration the caller already made, so a caller that imports first and then places cannot be given a second one; a caller with no declaration still gets one, which the second test pins. The lesson is the one this pass keeps recording in a new shape: moving a two-step into its owner is not the same as removing the callers step, and nothing failed until someone did the most ordinary thing in the product — import a file.

title: The editor says how much of the scene its artboard now holds

Fabric keeps its radius in step with scaleX and scaleY, so one dragged corner makes it an ellipse, and the selection inspector already said so — a circle, an ellipse and a triangle own NO shape-specific field, each is fully described by the width and height the general fields carry. title: Nothing anywhere says the document has unsaved changes
detail: MEASURED BY HUNTING FOR A SIGNAL THAT IS NOT THERE, which is the only way to measure an absence. There is a dedicated status element for it - footer.editor-shell-status, reading Fabric editor ready - so the affordance exists and is wired to something. It never changes. Select an object: still Fabric editor ready. Save to library: still Fabric editor ready. Type into the theme Name field and leave it unsaved, giving the document a real difference from what is on disk: still Fabric editor ready. Alongside it, the document title is Vigilia — editor with no asterisk and no suffix, no element carries a class matching /dirty|unsaved|modified/i anywhere in the tree, and the body text contains no unsaved marker. So an author who has just renamed their theme and typed a rectangle has no visible signal that anything is pending. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC COMPLAINT IS THE COMBINATION WITH vg-060, and the two together are worse than either alone. vg-060 is that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, so saved work disappears from view on reload. This is that nothing tells the author work is pending before they reload. An author renames a theme, adds a card, sees no dirty marker, closes the tab, reopens, and is looking at the Starter - with two independent signals that should have prevented it and neither present. There is a dirty key in the editor already: vg-026's own description records that isDirty is a string comparison against a key captured in the PersistenceManager constructor, and the Ctrl+N prompt consults it at editor-session.ts. So the state exists and is read in one place; it is simply never surfaced. The cheapest version of this fix is the status line the editor already has. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, because the fix does not work and the reason is worth the row. The obvious signal is save() in editor-shell, which is what every OBJECT manager calls, so I plumbed a document-change callback from it to the status bar and rendered Unsaved changes over the last message. Live, the status did not move: a nudge still read Fabric editor ready, and renaming the theme in the Name field still read Fabric editor ready, while Save to library correctly read Saved to library. So save() is NOT the funnel the rows hunt-by-hunting-for-a-signal assumed. There are at least THREE edit paths — object managers through save(), the nudge through the shortcut manager into canvas-nudge, and the theme and palette fields through their own panels commits — and only the first goes through it. The reason it matters: PersistenceManager.isDirty(current, assets) already answers this exactly, and the session already calls it, but only on the way to a replacement prompt. Wiring every edit path would duplicate a comparison that already exists; asking the session for the answer instead is the design question, not a patch. Reverted rather than shipped: a status bar that says Fabric editor ready while dirty would be worse than the current one, which at least says nothing false.

title: The browser will refresh or close with unsaved work and warn nobody
detail: RAISED BY THE USER, and confirmed by hand including a control that proves the measurement is sound rather than an automation blind spot. Select a palette token, click Import asset, choose one file - a real, unsaved change - then refresh. The page goes, 53 rows become 52, and nothing is said: no dialog, no status message, no prompt. Same on navigating away to another page. The obvious worry is that Chromium suppresses beforeunload dialogs under automation, which would make this unmeasurable here rather than absent. It is not: with a beforeunload handler installed by hand on the same page and the same harness, the reload DOES produce a dialog of type beforeunload and the harness records it. So the instrument can see exactly what the app is not producing, and the app produces none. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OBVIOUS: vg-060 already established that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, and vg-071 that nothing anywhere signals unsaved work. This is the third leg of the same shape, and it is the one that is nearly free to fix - a beforeunload listener reading the isDirty key the editor already computes. Note the browser owns that dialog's wording and gives no room to customise it, so if the product wants to say what would be lost rather than just ask, that is a deliberate design call rather than something beforeunload can do. Related: vg-071 and vg-060.

title: Reopening the editor discards saved work and shows the Starter instead
detail: MEASURED THREE WAYS, and it is the second half of vg-059's damage. Rename the theme through the theme-settings Name field from System dashboard to SENTINEL-9931 - the field reads SENTINEL-9931 and the host's document reads {"name":"SENTINEL-9931"}. Then reload the editor page. The Name field reads System dashboard again and the layer list is the Starter's 52 rows. The saved work is still on the host - it is the editor that does not open it. So the author's round trip is: edit, see it saved, close the tab, reopen, and be holding the Starter with no prompt and no warning that what they were working on is still there. NOT THE SAME AS vg-026: that row is the discard prompt appearing when it should not, and this is a document that never being loaded in the first place, so even discarding everything correctly would not help. THE ACTIVE THEME IS UNSET, which is where I would look first but have not established: /api/themes/active returns {"active":null} alongside the theme list, so nothing designates vigilia-demo-dashboard as what the editor should open, and Save to library evidently does not set it. Save to library, Release package and Open package are three different verbs in the File menu and only one of them is the one an author means by save. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: the editor does reach the library through File > Open library, so the path exists - what is missing is that the default open is the Starter rather than the author's own theme, and that Open library first raises the same spurious Save changes before opening another theme prompt that vg-026 is about. RE-CONFIRMED AT ITS STRONGEST, with the editor rebuilt and on the current mainline, and this time the work is a real object rather than a name. Rename the theme to MY-REAL-WORK, insert a Rectangle, File > Save to library: the host's document reads MY-REAL-WORK with 53 objects - the Starter's 52 plus the rectangle. Then reload the editor, which is what closing and reopening the tab does. The Name field reads System dashboard and the layer list shows 52 rows. The author's name is gone, their rectangle is gone, and nothing was said. This is the shape an author actually loses work in, and it is the same shape vg-071 makes invisible: there is no dirty marker to warn them before the reload (vg-071) and the reload itself discards the theme they were working on (this row). Together they are a session's work vanishing with no signal at either end. NOT THE DISCARD PROMPT and not the Starter's dirty-on-open state that vg-026 is about - I re-checked that guard this pass and it is correct, Ctrl+N on an untouched document goes straight to the size dialog and the prompt appears only after a real edit. The defect here is narrower and worse: the default document the editor opens is the template, not the author's own saved theme, and no part of the product says so.

title: The colour picker jumps to the top-left of the window the moment it is clicked
detail: RAISED BY THE USER and reproduced exactly, with the coordinates. Open the palette, select Frosted panel, click Pick a colour. title: The gradient control is confusing to use, and it discards the colour it replaces
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - the gradient control is very confusing to use - which is a judgement I am recording rather than contradicting, and which one measurement sharpens rather than settles. WHAT I COULD MEASURE is what the control does to an author's existing work. Select the Frosted panel token, which is a 30% alpha #0815234d used by eight objects, and switch Paint from Solid to Linear gradient. The panel gives Angle, Stop 1 position, Stop 1 colour, Stop 2 position, Stop 2 colour and Add stop, and it is usable - I typed 8-digit hex into a stop and it saved and rendered exactly - so this is not a report of a broken control. What it does is replace the token's colour with #ffffff and #000000, both fully opaque, and both defaults are unlike the colour they are replacing: a 30% frosted panel becomes an opaque black-to-white sweep across eight objects, from one dropdown choice, with the previous colour gone and only undo to get it back. The token row does say Frosted panel · 8, so the author has the count, and the defaults are a defensible starting point. But a gradient seeded with white and black is a colour nobody would have chosen for a frosted panel, and the control offers no starting-from-current behaviour, which is the one thing that would make it feel predictable. THE COMFUSION THE USER DESCRIBED MAY BE EXACTLY THIS and is worth naming rather than assuming: the first thing the control does to a colour is overwrite it with two unrelated colours. That is a design answer, not a defect, and it is the user's call - but the measurement is what an author meets first, and seeding from the current value costs nothing.

title: A pasted image is saved as a blob: URL and never becomes an asset, so it is gone everywhere else
detail: MEASURED END TO END, AND IT IS SILENT DATA LOSS. Put a PNG on the clipboard, click the canvas, press Ctrl+V. The image appears on the canvas at 0,0, is named Image, and the inspector shows it with a Crop button - the paste path itself works. Then File > Save to library. The saved document does contain an object named Image, and its src reads blob:http://127.0.0.1:5311/081c983e-cebf-4fd8-b75a-8d9a3e45bfc8. A blob URL is a handle into one browser session's memory; it means nothing in any other tab, any other browser, on a phone, or on a second visit.  HALF FIXED, AND THE REAL BLOCKER IS NOW NAMED. A pasted image took the HALF-ONLY PATH: the clipboard called imageManager.importImage and stopped, so the object kept the blob URL it was decoded from and nothing ever declared the bytes. The assets pane did both halves and the paste did not, which is why an asset import survives and a paste does not. AssetManager now owns both — placeImage declares the file AND puts it on the canvas — and the assets pane and a paste both go through it, so neither can take the half-only path again. The clipboard manager takes its importer from the session, which owns the asset manager; the shell builds it before that exists, so the importer is installed rather than injected. MEASURED on a pasted PNG: the saved envelope now declares assets/pasted-probe.png and the object carries vigiliaAsset {assetId pasted-probe, kind image}, which it did not before. STILL BROKEN, and this is the part that matters: the objects src STILL serialises as blob:http://... because NOTHING IN THE RENDERER RESOLVES vigiliaAsset. Searched every reader — the asset manager uses it to count references and to refuse removal, and scene-fabric only writes and reads it as a property; no adapter, scene or player path turns an assetId into a URL. So the bytes now ship and the image still does not travel, and the remaining fix is not in the editor at all: the scene has to resolve the reference the way it already resolves background media through createAssetResolver. Until that exists, a pasted image is a session handle with a copy of its bytes attached. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files. THE PLAYER HALF IS FIXED ON ba043ee AND THE ROW STAYS OPEN, because the editor half is worse than this row recorded. REPRODUCED FIRST, unchanged: paste a PNG (synthetic clipboard event carrying a 4x4 image), File > Save to library, and the host document declares assets/pasted-probe.png and assets/pasted-probe-2.png while both objects still carry src blob:http://127.0.0.1:8791/... . PLAYER, after ba043ee: at 390x839 a fresh load of that theme requests /api/themes/vigilia-demo-dashboard/assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png over HTTP and logs no error, where before it asked for the dead blob. The scene tests pin the rewrite and go red without it. EDITOR, and this is the finding worth carrying forward: reopening that same saved theme in the editor does not show a broken image, it DROPS THE OBJECT. 53 objects come back where the document holds 55, no object on the canvas carries vigiliaAsset at all, and the console shows ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on both blob URLs. Fabric enlivens from src alone, so a dead blob URL means the object is never created, which leaves AssetManager.hydrate - the thing that exists to revive exactly these images - with nothing to hydrate. The next save then writes 53 objects and the loss is permanent and silent. This row said the editor half was done and that the remaining fix was not in the editor; that is true of DECLARING the asset and not of surviving a reload. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: the resolver the editor needs is AssetManager.previewUrl, but the manager is a field of EditorSession constructed empty and loaded in its constructor, while the shell that revives the scene is mounted BEFORE the session exists - and the manager must hold this document's bytes before the revive, not after. Wiring it means moving the manager lifecycle out of the session into editor-main and adding it to EditorSessionOptions. That spans three owners and is a change of ownership rather than a patch, so it is recorded here rather than made inside the player fix. AND THE EDITOR HALF IS FIXED TOO, on dbde35a, so the paragraph above is the state of the finding before the fix rather than its final state. The ownership moved rather than being worked around: mountEditorShell revives the scene before a session exists, so the bytes have to be resolvable before EditorSession is constructed - and the session built its AssetManager as a field and loaded it in its own constructor, after. editor-main builds and loads one manager now, the first moment holding both the document and its bytes, and hands the same instance to the session; that left EditorSessionOptions.assets a second way to hand over the same bytes that nothing read, so it is gone. ON f3736ad THE URL IS ALSO STRIPPED FROM THE SAVE, which is what the paragraph above said was still shipping: Fabric writes src on every image whatever the caller asked for, and serialiseScene now takes it back off wherever the object carries vigiliaAsset - leaving an image with no reference alone, because it has nothing to resolve. THAT CHANGE HAD ONE MORE CONSEQUENCE, worth recording because it would have been a new silent loss one keystroke away: history serialises through the same serialiser and revived without a resolver, so a stripped src would have made every undo of a pasted image delete it. The history manager now revives through the same resolver the mount does. FINAL ROUND TRIP, one save and one reload of each: the document holds 55 objects with both pasted images carrying vigiliaAsset and no src, and the string blob: appears nowhere in the scene; the editor reopens at 55 with both images decoding at naturalWidth 4; the player fetches both assets over HTTP from that document; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y hold at 55 with both images decoding.
check: Both halves, measured against the numbers that proved them. RED, unchanged: a pasted PNG (synthetic clipboard event, 4x4) then File > Save to library declares assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png while both objects still save src blob:http://127.0.0.1:8791/... ; reopening that theme in the editor gave 53 objects and 53 layer rows where the document held 55, no object on the canvas carried vigiliaAsset, and the console reported ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on both blob URLs. GREEN, player (ba043ee): at 390x839 a fresh load requests /api/themes/vigilia-demo-dashboard/assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png over HTTP with no console error. GREEN, editor (dbde35a): the same theme reopens at 55 objects and 55 layer rows on two consecutive reloads, both images carry vigiliaAsset and both decode (naturalWidth 4), and Save to library writes a document of 55 with both references and both declared assets. Scene tests pin the revival rewrite and go red without it; the asset-manager test pins a reference with no bytes answering undefined rather than throwing. 2433 tests across 180 files.

title: The Language setting saves a locale that nothing ever reads
detail: WITHDRAWN — the finding's premise is wrong, and the user corrected it twice. Ruling 2026-10-01: "Language is only used for time text & external api sensor sources that return a text value, weather, for example", amended by: "what I meant for language is as a theme property: the author declared what language the theme was designed in. And it also govern datetime string render." THE ROW IS REFUTED BY A SPEC THAT WAS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, not by anything this session did: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-clock-and-theme-locale.md, status implemented, five days before the row was filed. The language is a fact about the theme, declared once by its author as metadata.locale — a BCP 47 tag beside name, author and description — so the theme reads in the language its author wrote it in and a library can filter on the fact. A v2 theme WITHOUT metadata.locale is refused, and so is a malformed or unrenderable tag: refused rather than degraded, so a theme never saves a language the runtime cannot show (fabric-envelope-validate.ts:126-151, owner themeLanguage at :121, whose own docblock names the failure mode it refuses — rendering "English behind the author's back"). The editor control ships as the spec asked: artboard-panel.ts has the curated-list select with the resolved month and weekday names shown live beside it, so the author sees words rather than a tag. WHAT THE ROW GOT WRONG, TWICE. First, it filed as its sharpest evidence that the player writes its own chrome in English in all fifteen locales — the one piece of text the product itself puts on the page. The spec answers that in its Non-goals: "Authoring copy for a theme's own labels. A theme's literal text is its text." The chrome is not what this property governs, so its being untranslated is correct, and translating it would have been the wrong fix. Second, it opened by claiming the setting "saves a locale nothing reads", which fc5c339 had already answered and the spec answers completely. The only half that was ever real is that a provider text value is not locale-formatted — and there is no such provider. formatTextReading at plan.ts:512 consults the locale only for a key the vocabulary marks instant, and every other text value is returned verbatim; today's text values are captions of identity (CPU manufacturer/brand/model at library.ts:497-516, GPU and drive names at lhm.ts:273 and library.ts:401) plus the clock's ISO instant. Weather is a future roadmap feature with no design, named in the spec only so that a later locale-aware provider reads the same declared fact. AN AGENT WAS DISPATCHED TO LOOK FOR IT BEFORE THE SPEC WAS READ. It wrote nothing and stood down, but the dispatch was the error and it is recorded here so the next one is not repeated: this repo had settled the question five days earlier and one reading of docs/superpowers/specs/ would have caught it.

title: The editor still does not refit the theme when the window is resized
detail: FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT SURVIVED THE FIX FOR vg-068, and measured by hand rather than taken from the agent's report. Open the editor at 2048 wide and the zoom badge reads 83%. Resize the window to 1600 and it reads 83%; to 1280, still 83%; to 1024, still 83%. One number across a 1024-pixel change, while the canvas behind it goes 1394, 946, 626, 370. Click Zoom to fit at that last size and the badge reads 22% - so the fit calculation is right and something else has to ask for it. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT IS WHICH EVENT FIRES THE REFIT. cde9aa6 made a PANEL COLLAPSE refit, and that works: at 1024, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the zoom 22% to 39%. A WINDOW RESIZE is a different event and did not get the same treatment. This is the half that matters in ordinary use, because a deliberate panel toggle is rare and resizing a window - or opening it at a size and keeping it - is what everyone does. An author whose window is not the width they opened the editor at spends the session looking at a theme at the wrong zoom inside a black field, and the badge reads a confident number throughout. Nothing recomputes on resize; only the click recomputes it. A ResizeObserver already exists on the body in this app for other purposes, so the seam is present. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, and the reason it was reverted is the useful part. CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS FILED: at 2048 the badge reads 83% with the canvas at 1394; resize to 1024 and it still reads 83% with the canvas at 370, and the artboard still starts at x 98, so 1290 of its 1388 pixels run off the right edge. Zoom to fit at that size gives 22%, so the fit exists — it is just not automatic. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Holding the zoom and re-centring the translation on every resize does exactly what the row wants — measured, at 370 the board then spans -512 to 882 against a 370 canvas, so it is centred and the rest is reachable by panning — and it BREAKS keeps the point under the cursor fixed while zooming, which resize() calls on construction and on every host size change. Panning to inspect a corner and then any resize, spurious or not, yanks the camera back to centre. That test failing is the finding, not an accident of the harness. So the question is not how to re-centre but WHEN: only when the camera was showing the whole board, so an authors pan survives and a fitted view follows the window. That needs a condition on the previous camera state — was it fitted or contained — which the viewport does not currently keep. Reverted rather than shipped: a camera that cannot be left where the author put it is a worse defect than one that leaves part of the board off the edge.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8799, resizing the window with the camera untouched since mount: the zoom badge read 83% at 2048, 57% at 1600, 37% at 1280 and 22% at 1024 as the canvas went 1394, 946, 626, 370 - one number per width, where every width read 83% before. Then the inverse, which is the invariant the reverted attempt broke: zoomed off fit to 19% and resized 2048 to 1280 and on to 1600, the badge held 19% at all three. Clicked Zoom to fit, back to 57%, and a further resize to 1400 refitted it to 45%.

title: A chart's aspect ratio changes its height but the inspector's Height field never updates
detail: MEASURED AS A DIRECT COMPARISON after a wrong first reading, which is worth recording because it nearly cost this row. I first concluded the three ratio buttons did nothing: geometry stayed 963x215 through 3:1, 4:1 and 2:1, and the buttons had no aria-pressed, no class and no computed-style difference. Both halves of that were instrument error. The style half: the screenshot showed 3:1 boxed after I had clicked 4:1, and I had sampled backgroundColor, which is rgb(245, 241, 232) on all three - the visible box is the focus ring, and there is genuinely no selected state. The effect half: I read the chart before saving, so the document had not caught up. THE FEATURE WORKS. Save after each click and the host's document gives the truth: 4:1 takes the height 215 to 241, 3:1 to 321, 2:1 to 482, all at width 963 - exactly the ratios named. THE DEFECT IS THE INSPECTOR DISAGREES WITH ALL OF IT. Across every click the Height field in the selection inspector reads 215, unchanged, while the object it is describing is 241, then 321, then 482. Four consecutive comparisons, mismatch on every one. So an author sets 2:1, watches the chart double in height, and reads a Height field that still says 215 - and the canvas dock and the field that owns the geometry are telling them two different things about the same object. That is the same class as the layer list disagreeing with the document, and it is the more dangerous of the two here, because the Height field is editable: an author who reads 215, believes it, and types a height is editing against a number the product no longer holds. The second half is small and cheap and worth doing alongside: nothing in the control group says which ratio is active - no aria-pressed on any of the three, no class, no style difference at all - so after clicking there is no way to tell 2:1 was applied from 3:1.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, with network-chart selected at W 430: clicking 4:1 put Height at 108, 3:1 at 143 and 2:1 at 215, each the width over its ratio, where the field read 215 through all three before. aria-pressed followed at every step - 4:1 true, then 3:1 true with the others false, then 2:1 true with the others false - where no button carried any pressed state at all before.
